text: Here is the curve f of x equals x squared.
caption: Here is the curve f(x) = x squared

text: A derivative measures how steep a curve is at a single point.
Take the point where x equals one, which sits at height one.
Slope means rise over run, and that needs two points, not one.
So add a second point, a little further along the curve.
The horizontal gap between the two points is called h.
The line through both points is called a secant line.
Its slope is the change in f, divided by the step h.
Right now h is one, so the second point sits at two.
The rise is three over a run of one, so the slope is three.
Now shrink h to one half, pulling the second point closer.
The rise is one point two five, so the slope is two point five.
caption: The rise is 1.25, so the slope is 2.5

text: Shrink h again, to one quarter, and the secant tilts further.
Now the slope is two point two five, still falling.
caption: Now the slope is 2.25, still falling

text: Shrink h to one tenth, and the two points almost touch.
The slope is now two point one, only just above two.
caption: The slope is now 2.1, only just above 2

text: In every row, the slope is exactly two plus h.
Squaring one plus h gives one, plus two h, plus h squared.
The ones cancel, and dividing by h leaves two plus h.
As h shrinks toward zero, two plus h closes in on two.
The secant turns into the tangent, which just touches the curve here.
That limiting slope, two, is the derivative of f at one.
At this point, the curve climbs two units for every one across.
In general, the derivative is the limit of the secant slope.
Doing this at every x gives the derivative two x.
caption: Doing this at every x gives the derivative 2x

text: A derivative is a secant slope, as the gap shrinks to zero.
